faq.metaDescription: Answers about stage payments, land paperwork, power of attorney and how to follow your home's progress from the United States.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: If your question isn't here, message us on WhatsApp. We reply within one business day.

secure.q: How do I know my money is safe?
secure.a: You never prepay the whole build. You sign a contract before the first payment, then pay for each stage only once you see the previous one finished, with photos and videos. All payments go to company accounts and come with a receipt.

stages.a: You make a down payment when you sign, which covers permits and design. The build is split into stages: foundation, walls, roof, utilities, finishes and handover. Before each stage we show you the previous one finished, and then you make that payment.

howToPay.q: How do I pay from the United States?
howToPay.a: From your US bank account, to an account in the company's name. When you sign, we explain the payment methods available. We will never ask you to deposit into a person's account.

finalPrice.a: It's an estimate based on reference prices. The final price is set in the contract after we check your land, and it doesn't change unless you ask for changes.

duration.a: It depends on the size of the home: a 2-bedroom home takes about 18 weeks and a two-story one about 30. The quote tool gives you the approximate time for each stage.

seeProgress.q: How do I see the progress from the United States?
seeProgress.a: Every week your project manager uploads dated photos and videos to your private portal. You can also ask for a video call from the site.

changes.q: Can I change something during the build?
changes.a: Yes. Changes are quoted separately and added to the contract before they're made, so you always know what they cost.

family.q: Can my family in Honduras supervise the build?
family.a: Yes. You can invite a relative to see the updates in the portal and confirm material deliveries. You decide whether they can also see payments and documents.

travel.q: Do I have to travel to Honduras to buy or build?
travel.a: No. Everything can be done from the United States. To sign deeds, you can give a power of attorney to someone you trust in Honduras.

powerOfAttorney.q: What is a power of attorney and do I need one?
powerOfAttorney.a: It's a document that authorizes someone you trust to sign for you in Honduras. You get it at the nearest Honduran consulate. You need it to sign a deed without traveling.

verifyTitle.q: How do I know the land has a clear title?
verifyTitle.a: Before any payment we show you the deed registered with the Property Institute and the lien-free certificate, which confirms the land has no debts or mortgages.

whereWork.q: Which departments do you work in?
whereWork.a: For now, Cortés, Francisco Morazán, Atlántida and Comayagua. If your land is in another department, message us: we're growing.

how.metaDescription: The full process to buy or build your home in Honduras from the United States: contract, stage payments, photo updates and clear paperwork.
how.title: How it works
how.intro: From the first quote to the keys. No surprises, and your money always in sight.

quote.title: Get a quote online
quote.body: Choose land, model, finishes and extras. You instantly see the estimated price, the payment plan and the timeline.

call.title: Video call
call.body: We review your land, your questions and the paperwork. If you don't have land, we show you options.

contract.title: Contract and down payment
contract.body: You sign the contract with the final price, stages, timelines and guarantees. The down payment starts the permits.

permits.title: Design and permits
permits.body: We finish the plans and get the building permit from the municipality.

build.title: Construction in stages
build.body: Every week we upload photos and videos to your portal. Before each stage you see the previous one finished and make that payment.

delivery.title: Handover
delivery.body: We walk through the house with you or your relative, fix anything needed and hand you the keys.

how.paymentsBody: You never prepay the whole build. You make a down payment when you sign and then one payment per stage, only once you see the previous one finished.
how.paymentsExample: Example with a $45,000 home and a 20% down payment: you pay $9,000 when you sign. When you see the permits done, you pay for the foundation. When you see the foundation finished, you pay for the walls. And so on until handover.
how.contractBody: The contract states the final price, what each stage includes, how long it takes, what happens if there's a delay and which guarantees you have. We send it to you before signing so you can review it calmly.
how.guaranteesBody: Construction guarantees are written into the contract. The exact terms will be published here before launch.
how.legalIntro: Buying or building in Honduras from abroad involves paperwork. We guide you through each step.

title.title: The deed
title.body: It's the document that makes you the owner. We check with you that it's registered with the Property Institute and that the land has no debts.

power.title: The power of attorney
power.body: If you can't travel, you give a power of attorney at the consulate to someone you trust so they can sign for you.

registry.title: The registration
registry.body: After signing, the deed in your name is registered with the Property Institute. We send you a copy.

how.familyTitle: Your family, with you at the site
how.familyBody: You can invite a relative in Honduras to your portal: they see the updates, can visit the site and confirm material deliveries.

trust.metaDescription: How we protect your money: a contract before we start, stage payments, reviewed paperwork and company accounts only.
trust.title: Why trust us
trust.intro: We know how hard every dollar is to earn and how hard it is to trust from far away. These are our rules.

promises.contract: We sign a contract with you before receiving any payment.
promises.stages: We charge for each stage only when you see it finished.
promises.photos: We send you photos and videos of your build every week.
promises.documents: We show you the property paperwork before any payment.
promises.receipts: We give you a receipt for every payment.

never.personal: Ask you to deposit into a person's account.
never.upfront: Charge you for the whole build up front.
never.permits: Start building without a municipal permit.
never.hidden: Add costs that aren't in the contract.
